children: The upcoming SUV will offer six airbags as standard, with bookings open at Rs 11,000 ahead of its 26 October launch

Hyundai Motor India has outlined the safety features of its upcoming Bayon SUV ahead of its launch on 26 October 2026. The model will feature 23 advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) functions, alongside a reinforced body structure and more than 35 safety features offered as standard across variants.
Built on Hyundai’s Global K Enhanced Platform, the Bayon uses four grades of high-strength steel, which account for 69 per cent of its body structure, according to the company.
Hyundai says the structure is designed to manage crash energy and improve occupant protection.

The SUV will be powered by a 1.5-litre four-cylinder petrol engine producing 115 PS and 143.8 Nm of torque. Buyers will be able to choose between a six-speed manual gearbox and an intelligent variable transmission (IVT).

The Bayon’s Hyundai SmartSense Level 2 Pro ADAS package includes forward collision avoidance assist, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot collision warning, and rear cross-traffic collision avoidance assist.
The system also includes highway driving assist and smart cruise control with stop-and-go functionality.
Three radars and 12 parking sensors support the driver assistance package.

Other equipment includes six airbags, electronic stability control, hill-start assist, rear parking sensors, tyre pressure monitoring and ISOFIX child-seat mounts. A surround-view monitor and blind-spot view monitor are also part of the safety package.
Hyundai says the vehicle offers more than 80 advanced safety features in total.
The availability of certain ADAS functions may vary by variant and operating conditions.
The Bayon will be available in 10 exterior colour options, including monotone, matte and dual-tone finishes. These include Atlas White, Fiery Red, Classy Blue and Titanium Black.
Bookings are open through Hyundai’s website and authorised dealerships for Rs 11,000. The company has yet to announce delivery timelines.
